# ![](https://commonwealth-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/11a6de77-d155-4f27-838d-0a995f6f8e64.1664277111137)**Proposal: Richard Welsh, Edgeware R&D August / September invoice 3 (Post paid)**

**Date 13th October 2022**

## **Introduction**
I’ve used this proposal and process to trial a new structure for people to run through that is simple, easy to understand and generalisable to all domains. 

It seemed only fair that I use my own proposal to dogfood, what is effectively my own suggestion. 

It aims to standardises timelines, responses and to ensure better communication for **voters** and **proposers** alike.

This approach is, as the overall proposal, a work in progress, so consider this an emerging set of standards, that will only work, if we all agree to try it. 

It starts with a very simple idea - a proposal has 3 clear stages **DRAFT**, **REVIEW** and **FINAL.**

_It is also rooted in a another simple but obvious point - _**Proposers** and **Voters** each have power, authority, responsibilities and duties that should be _understood_, _accepted_ and actioned. 

## **3 week proposal process for content**

**WEEK 1**

_Proposal team responsibilities: _

- **Version 1: **submit **DRAFT** proposal for REVIEW
- DRAFT can be provocative - designed to elicit a strong response
- DRAFT can pose questions - designed to solicit responses
- DRAFT can ask for help - designed to encourage collaboration
- Engage in discussion, respond clearly and calmly and debate the content not the people
- Keep an open mind and treat this as a collaborative process


_Voter responsibilities: _

- 1 week of discussion, comment and responses
- Questions and comments should be clear and considerate 
- Keep an open mind and treat this as a collaborative process 


**WEEK 2 **

_Proposal team responsibilities:_

- **Version 2: **submit** REVIEW **proposal taking into account DRAFT comments
- REVIEW aims to meaningfully evolve the DRAFT
- REVIEW aims to include responses to questions as Q&
